plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with large daisy-like flower heads made of golden ray florets surrounding a dark central disk. Young flower heads track the sun across the sky, and the plant is widely grown for seed, oil, and ornament.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early fall in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to North America; cultivated across the United States, Europe, Ukraine, Russia, and Argentina
plants.funFact: The sunflower head is actually a composite of hundreds to thousands of tiny individual flowers arranged in a Fibonacci spiral pattern.

plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: An aromatic evergreen shrub with silvery-gray foliage and slender spikes of fragrant purple flowers. It thrives in sunny, well-drained soils and is a magnet for bees and butterflies.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring through late summer; peak bloom in July in many regions
plants.location: Native to the Mediterranean; grown in Provence (France), England, Bulgaria, Tasmania, and the western United States
plants.funFact: The name lavender likely derives from the Latin 'lavare' meaning 'to wash', as Romans used it to scent baths.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: An aquatic perennial with large, round, water-repellent leaves held above the water and spectacular, fragrant flowers on tall stalks. Blooms open in the morning and close by afternoon over several days.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer, peaking July to August in temperate Asia
plants.location: Asia and northern Australia, including India, China, Japan, and Vietnam; cultivated in ponds worldwide
plants.funFact: Lotus flowers can regulate their temperature to about 30-35°C (86-95°F), even when the surrounding air is much cooler, and lotus seeds can remain viable for over a thousand years.

plants.name: Epilobium angustifolium
plants.description: A tall perennial wildflower forming dense stands of spiky magenta flower clusters, often colonizing burned or cleared land. Flowers open from the bottom of the spike upward as summer progresses.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early fall; peaks around late July in northern latitudes
plants.location: Northern temperate and subarctic regions including Alaska, Canada, Scandinavia, Siberia, and the northern United States
plants.funFact: Locals often say that when the fireweed blooms reach the top of the stalk, summer is nearly over and winter is about six weeks away.
